en: Herr Krug's philosophical endeavours divide of themselves into two sides, the one of which is turned polemically against transcendental idealism, while the other concerns his own philosophical convictions, as Herr Krug calls them.
zh: 克鲁格先生的哲学努力本身分成两面：一面是论战性地针对先验观念论，另一面则涉及他自己的哲学信念——如克鲁格先生所称的那样。

en: As for Herr Krug's polemical procedure, the standpoint that he gives himself against the Doctrine of Science is to be the standpoint of scepticism, S. 5, preface, and indeed in such a way as befits scepticism, that Herr Krug argues not from his own convictions (why not, will emerge on the occasion of the Letters on Transcendental Idealism and especially of the Organon, where the author sets out his own convictions), but from the Doctrine of Science itself, and Herr Krug thinks that a scientific investigation is to be introduced by his Letters.
With regard to the subjective manner of the utterance, it is a true delight to hear the author's sobriety, fairness, and uprightness speak.

“The Doctrine of Science”, he says, “has, to be sure, hitherto behaved rather standoffishly and has rebuked its opponents, for the most part, in a somewhat rough tone; meanwhile, it also cannot be denied that it has, in many cases, merely used the right of retaliation, and, if in doing so it has here and there overstepped the limits of that right, this may perhaps stem more from the fullness of strength with which it entered the battlefield than from a hostile disposition”.100) The author has “hitherto taken no part in this dispute, because he held it a duty first to examine a system more closely for himself before coming forward with a public examination”.

With the noble and beneficent consciousness of this fulfilled duty, he now treats “the Doctrine of Science with the respect due to it, has opposed to it not hateful inferences but grounds, and fears, if he is not entirely mistaken in his opponents, no opposite treatment, for he has far too favourable an opinion of them not to hope to be treated on a different footing than” etc. “Should he, however, find himself deceived in his hope, he will give up his investigations; the upright and worthy reason for this is that from a literary feud conducted with passionate heat something clever seldom comes, and in the end the spectators are given only a scandal that brings science together with its cultivators (among whom Herr Krug also counts himself) into public discredit.”
zh: 至于克鲁格先生的论战做法，他给自己设立的反对《知识学》的立足点应当是怀疑论的立足点，S. 5，前言，而且应当像怀疑论所应有的那样，即克鲁格先生不是从自己的信念出发（为什么不这样，等到《先验观念论书信》、尤其等到《工具论》——作者在那里陈述自己的信念——的时候自会明白），而是从《知识学》本身出发来论证；克鲁格先生还认为，一项科学的检验应当由他的书信来引出。
就表达的主观方式而言，听这位作者先生的清醒、公允和正直说话，真是一大乐事。
“《知识学》”，他说，“迄今固然表现得相当不好打交道，而且多半用一种不太温和的语调教训它的对手；不过也不能否认，它在有些场合只是用了报复的权利，而如果说它这样做时偶尔越出了这种权利的界限，那也许更多是出于它踏上战场时的力量充沛，而不是出于敌意。”100) 作者“迄今没有参与这场争论，因为他认为有义务先把一个体系为自己更仔细地检验一番，然后才带着公开的检验出场”。

带着这种履行了义务的高尚而善良的意识，他现在“以《知识学》应得的敬重对待它，对它提出的不是可憎的推论，而是根据，并且，只要他没有完全看错自己的对手，就不担心受到相反方式的对待，因为他对他们的看法太好，不会不指望受到另一种待遇”等等。“不过，如果他发现自己的指望落了空，他就会放弃自己的研究；其正直而可敬的理由是：一场带着狂热激情进行的文字争斗，很少能弄出什么聪明的东西，最后只是给旁观者一场丑闻，使科学连同它的培育者（克鲁格先生也把自己算在里面）在公众面前声名扫地。”

en: In the first Letter Herr Krug recounts what he finds to approve of in transcendental idealism; he declares at S. 14 that he does not find the I at all so ridiculous or so unthinkable as some seem to find it; what then, he asks, absurd lies in it, what could force a laugh, or even only a smile, from a sensible man, if I simply call I what I think through the abstrakzion (so Herr Krug spells it) from everything that does not belong to myself? – he also finds the demand very well grounded: “Attend to yourself, turn your gaze away from everything that surrounds you and into your inner being.”101) – further, he also has nothing against it, etc., and finally he also cannot hold idealism as a philosophical theory to be as dangerous as it seems to be held by many.

On these sides he would know nothing to set against transcendental idealism (thus Herr Krug declines it: dem Organisme, dem Dogmatisme; in the genitive: des Idealismes, des Organismes, des Realismes, etc.); whether it has no other exposed spots, however, will show itself in what follows.
zh: 在第一封信里，克鲁格先生讲述他在先验观念论身上认可什么；他在 S. 14 声明，他完全不觉得自我像有些人似乎觉得的那样可笑、那样不可设想；他问：如果我把通过 Abstrakzion（克鲁格先生就是这样拼写的）撇开一切不属于我自己的东西所想到的东西径直称为我，这里面究竟有什么荒唐之处，竟能逼得一个明事理的人发笑，哪怕只是微微一笑呢？——他还觉得那个要求大有根据：“注意你自己，把你的目光从你周围的一切转开，转向你的内心。”101)——此外他也不反对，等等；最后他也认为观念论作为一种哲学理论并不像许多人似乎认为的那样危险。
从这些方面，他对先验观念论（克鲁格先生是这样变格的：dem Organisme，dem Dogmatisme；属格：des Idealismes，des Organismes，des Realismes，等等）提不出什么反对意见；不过它是否在别处没有破绽，下面自会显示。

en: That in which Herr Krug bestows his approval on transcendental idealism makes up the content of the first Letter; but this conceited and self-satisfied tone of justice and sobriety, and this tediousness of manner, runs through the whole.
zh: 克鲁格先生对先验观念论表示赞许的那些内容，构成了第一封信的内容；但这种自命公正清醒的狂妄自满腔调，以及这种手法的乏味，却贯穿了全书。

en: But what Herr Krug brings forward against the Doctrine of Science, and what he at S. 79 calls a detailed examination, runs from S. 24-52, for in the third Letter he has to do only with the names of idealism, dogmatism, and realism; “to be sure, in the main matter it does not depend on the names, but through the opposition of dogmatism the staff has, as it were, already been broken in advance over each and every opponent of the Doctrine of Science, and precisely thereby all access to the spirit of impartial examination, to which it has after all been summoned so often and so emphatically, is if not barred then made difficult”. – In order now to avert such a danger, Herr Krug divides dogmatism in a material respect into idealism, which denies the reality of the external world, and realism, if it admits and asserts that reality; – but in this division precisely transcendental idealism is left out, for this does not merely admit – for an admitting is not what is at issue in philosophical systems – but asserts the reality of the external world just as much as its ideality, and the theoretical part of the Doctrine of Science aims at nothing other than a deduction of the reality of the external world.
zh: 不过克鲁格先生用来反对《知识学》的东西，以及他在 S. 79 称为详尽检验的东西，是从 S. 24-52 开始的，因为在第三封信里他打交道的只是观念论、独断论和实在论这些名称；“主要的事情固然不在于名称，但通过对独断论的对立，可以说事先就已经对《知识学》的所有一切对手作了判决，而正因如此，那条通往不偏不倚的检验精神的道路——对这种方法《知识学》毕竟是那样频繁、那样着力地提出过要求——即使没有被完全封死，也变得难以通行”。——为了避开这种危险，克鲁格先生从质料方面把独断论分为观念论，即否认外部世界实在性的那种，以及实在论，即承认并主张那种实在性的那种；——但在这种划分里，恰恰把先验观念论漏掉了，因为先验观念论不只是承认——在哲学体系里根本谈不上什么承认——而是既主张外部世界的实在性，也同样主张它的观念性，而《知识学》的理论部分所指向的，无非是对外部世界实在性的演绎。

en: The detailed examination itself (S. 24-52) of the Doctrine of Science is directed against a single point; Herr Krug cannot, namely, endure the limitedness of the I: the I is supposed to limit itself, and indeed not by freedom and arbitrariness (a good pairing), but in accordance with an immanent law of its own essence; and yet the ground of authentication of transcendental idealism supposedly rests on the interest of self-sufficiency; and I too, says Herr Krug, am, together with the friend to whom he addresses these Letters and with the author of the Doctrine of Science, very much interested in my self-sufficiency; that Fichte has associated himself with Herr Krug and his friend as a joint interested party in Herr Krug's self-sufficiency, as Herr Krug here relates, has otherwise not been known to the public.
For the interest of this self-sufficiency, however, it is supposedly completely indifferent whether the I acts necessarily as it acts through its outer or through an inner nature.

Herr Krug compares the I that acts from inner natural necessity and the I that is determined by a nature outside us, the latter with a mere flute that an artist plays, the former with a flute-clock that produces harmonious tones through itself.
zh: 《知识学》的那番详尽检验本身（S. 24-52）只针对一个点；克鲁格先生不能忍受自我的受限制：自我据说要限制自己，而且不是凭自由和任意（一个很好的搭配），而是依照它自己本质的一种内在规律；可是先验观念论的验证根据据说就在于独立自主这一旨趣；克鲁格先生说，我和他这些书信所寄的那位朋友，以及和《知识学》的作者一样，也非常关心我的独立自主；至于费希特像克鲁格先生这里所讲的那样，与克鲁格先生及其朋友结成了对克鲁格先生独立自主的共同关切者，公众此前并不知情。
但就这种独立自主的旨趣而言，自我究竟是凭自己的外部自然还是凭一种内部自然而必然地像它那样行动，据说是完全无所谓的。
克鲁格先生把出于内部自然必然性而行动的自我，和由我们之外的一种自然所规定的自我加以比较：后者好比一支由艺术家吹奏的普通笛子，前者好比一架靠自己发出和谐音调的笛钟。

en: From this it supposedly follows, then presumably also sufficiently, that the dutifulness of the idealistic way of thinking is not meant so seriously; with every philosophical theory a good will and a moral disposition can be connected.
(By contrast, the anthropomorphism of the imagination, polytheism, at S. 112, is for him an all the worse abomination; he declares it to be utterly incompatible with morality.)

Although, now, the interest of self-sufficiency is not sufficiently satisfied by transcendental idealism, yet for the speculative interest of reason an extraordinary amount is gained; here all is light and clarity, the I lets everything arise before its eyes and sees it arise; but the main task is after all not solved.

Herr Krug, namely, sees two human beings, a European and a Moor, and feels compelled to represent the one to himself with white, the other with black skin colour; or he would like to save a human being from a danger to life, but the floods rage or the flames blaze, etc., – in the incomprehensibility of the limits the Doctrine of Science supposedly gets stuck, as in all likelihood all philosophy does.
zh: 由此想必也就充分说明，观念论思维方式的那种合乎义务并不是那么认真的；任何一种哲学理论都可以与善良意志和道德意向结合在一起。
（与此相反，想象力的拟人化，即多神论，S. 112，对他说来倒是更加可恶的丑事；他宣称它与道德完全不能相容。）
尽管独立自主的旨趣通过先验观念论并未得到充分满足，但对理性的思辨旨趣来说却获益极多；这里一切都是光明和清晰，自我让一切在它眼前产生，并且看见一切产生；不过主要任务毕竟还没有解决。
克鲁格先生据说是看见两个人，一个欧洲人和一个摩尔人，于是不得不把前者表象为白皮肤、后者表象为黑皮肤；或者他想把一个人从生命危险中救出来，但洪水汹涌或烈火肆虐，等等，——在界限的不可理解性里，《知识学》据说是卡住了，而照一切推测，一切哲学也都卡在那里。

en: The last letter, in which Herr Krug, concerning the agreement or non-agreement of the Kantian system, fairly and cleverly opines that it would presumably be best to refrain for the present entirely from judging this matter, Herr Krug closes with the word:
zh: 最后一封信里，克鲁格先生就康德体系是否一致，颇为公道而聪明地认为，在这件事上暂时最好完全不作判断，这封信克鲁格先生是用这样一句话收尾的：

en: keep the lazy herd of drones away from the hives,102)
zh: ignavum fucos pecus a praesepibus arce,102)（把懒惰的雄蜂群挡在蜂房之外）

en: which after all still fits many a one whom Herr Krug was not thinking of when he wrote it down.
zh: 而这句话大概也还适用于某些人，克鲁格先生写下它的时候并没有想到这些人。

en: Of quite the same content is the polemical side of the Letters on the most recent idealism, which are directed against Schelling's system of transcendental philosophy, — only the author says in the preface that he has gone one step further here with regard to the open exposition of his own convictions.
zh: 《论最新观念论的书信》中论战的那一面，内容完全一样，这些书信是针对谢林的先验哲学体系而发的——只不过作者在序言里说，他在这里就公开陈述自己的信念而言，已经多走了一步。

en: To the openness of the exposition it will also have to be counted that Herr Krug here advances his objections more boldly and in Schelling's system — why Herr Krug may call him our transcendental idealist is really impossible to see — demonstrates unforgivable inconsistencies, palpable contradictions, nonsense, etc.
zh: 陈述的公开性还得算上一点：克鲁格先生在这里把自己的反驳提得更大胆，并且在谢林的体系里——克鲁格先生为什么偏要把他称作我们那位先验观念论者，实在看不出来——指出了一些不可原谅的前后不一、明摆着的矛盾、胡说等等。

en: Concerning the original boundedness, some light seems to have dawned on Herr Krug from the construction of the modes of action of the I out of opposed activities or out of the original difference, and concerning the absolute necessity of positing reason as subject and object and thereby limitation, Herr Krug does not let himself be heard further.
But all the more he now holds to the determinacy that is admitted to be the unexplainable and incomprehensible element of philosophy.
zh: 关于原初的受限性，克鲁格先生似乎从自我以对立的活动、或从最初的差别来建构自己的行动方式中，见到了一些光亮；而关于把理性设定为主体兼客体、并因此设定限制的那种绝对必然性，克鲁格先生就不再作声了。
但他现在越发抓住那个规定性不放，据说这个规定性被承认为哲学中无法解释、无法理解的东西。

en: In the first place he finds it contradictory that in philosophy absolutely nothing is to be presupposed and yet the absolute A = A, as absolute identity and as difference, out of which all limitation is constructed, is presupposed.
zh: 首先他觉得这是矛盾的：在哲学里根本不该有任何东西被预设，可是绝对者 A = A，作为绝对同一性和作为差别——一切限制性都由此建构出来——却还是被预设了。

en: This contradiction is precisely the one that common understanding will always find in philosophy; common understanding places the absolute and the finite on exactly the same rank and extends the demands that are made with regard to the finite to the absolute.

So it is demanded in philosophy that nothing should be put forward unproved; common understanding at once finds the inconsistency that has been committed, it finds that the absolute has not been proved; - with the idea of the absolute its being is supposed to be posited immediately, but, common understanding knows how to object, it can very well think something, form an idea of something, without its being necessary on that account that this thought something at the same time has a determinate being, etc. Thus Herr Krug will object to geometry that it is not a science complete in itself, as it claims, for it does not after all prove the determinate being of an infinite space in which it draws its lines. - Or does Herr Krug take God or the absolute for a kind of hypothesis that philosophy allows itself to be guilty of, as one physics permits itself the hypothesis of an empty space, of a magnetic, electric matter, etc., in whose place another physics can again put other hypotheses?
zh: 这个矛盾恰恰就是庸常知性在哲学里总会找到的那个矛盾；庸常知性把绝对者和有限者完全放在同一个等级上，并把针对有限者提出的要求扩展到绝对者身上。

于是在哲学里就有这样的要求：不该有任何未加证明的东西被摆出来；庸常知性立刻发现已经犯下的不一贯，它发现人们并没有证明绝对者；——据说有了绝对者的观念，它的存在就直接被设定了，可是庸常知性懂得反驳说，它完全可以想某个东西、对某个东西形成观念，而并不因此就必然使这个被想到的东西同时也拥有定在，等等。这样，克鲁格先生就会指责几何学并不像它自己声称的那样是一门自身完成了的科学，因为它毕竟没有证明一个无限空间——它把自己的线画在这个空间里——的定在。——或者，克鲁格先生是把上帝或绝对者当成一种哲学硬要让自己犯下的假设，就像某一种物理学允许自己假设虚空、假设磁性的、电的质料等等，而另一种物理学又可以拿另一些假设来替换它们那样吗？

en: The second inconsistency that strikes Herr Krug is that it has been promised that the whole system of our representations should be deduced; and although he has himself found a passage in the transcendental idealism in which the sense of this promise is expressly explained, he still cannot refrain from once again quite forgetting that here it is philosophy that is being spoken of.

Herr Krug cannot refrain from understanding the matter like the commonest mob and demanding that every dog and cat, indeed even Herr Krug's pen, should be deduced, and since this does not happen, he thinks the labouring mountain and the tiny, tiny mouse must occur to his friend; one should not have given oneself the appearance of wanting to deduce the whole system of representations.
zh: 让克鲁格先生注意到的第二个不一贯是：有人许诺过，我们表象的整个体系应当被演绎出来；尽管他自己在《先验观念论体系》里已经找到一处，那里明确解释了这一许诺的含义，他还是忍不住又一次完全忘掉，这里谈的是哲学。
克鲁格先生忍不住像最庸俗的群氓那样去理解这件事，并要求把每一只狗和猫、甚至克鲁格先生的那支笔都演绎出来；既然这件事没有发生，他就认为他的朋友该想到那临产的群山和那只小得不能再小的老鼠；本来就不该摆出一副要把表象的整个体系演绎出来的架势。

en: It is comical how Herr Krug is after all so gracious as not to want to take the philosopher, who gives himself the appearance of a master in philosophy, so strictly at his word; instead he demands only a little, only the deduction of one determinate representation, e.g. the moon with all its marks, or a rose, a horse, a dog, or wood, iron, clay, an oak, or even only of his pen.

It looks as if Herr Krug wanted with such demands to make the matter easy for the idealist, in that he has set him only a subordinate point of the solar system, the moon, or, as something still much easier, his pen.

But does Herr Krug not comprehend that the determinacies that are incomprehensible in transcendental idealism belong to the philosophy of nature, of whose difference from transcendental idealism he seems to know nothing at all, insofar as they - as is not the case with Herr Krug's pen - can be spoken of in philosophy?
In it he can find a deduction (a word whose meaning is as little fit here as its orthography) of one of those things that he proposes, of iron.

Does Herr Krug then have so little a concept of philosophical construction as to think that the moon could be comprehended without the whole solar system, and does he have so weak a representation of this solar system as not to see that the cognition of this system is the most sublime and highest task of reason?

If Herr Krug had of the greatness of this determinate task, or if he had of that which at the present moment is primarily the interest of philosophy, namely once again to place God absolutely first, at the head of philosophy, as the sole ground of everything, as the single principium essendi and cognoscendi, after one has placed him long enough beside other finitudes or quite at the end as a postulate that proceeds from an absolute finitude, - if he had a distant inkling of this, how could it occur to him to demand of philosophy the deduction of his pen?

A dog, an oak, a horse, a reed are indeed, just as a Moses, Alexander, Cyrus, Jesus, etc., something more excellent, and both series of organizations lie closer to philosophy than Herr Krug's pen and the philosophical works composed with it; the philosophy of nature points out to him how he has to comprehend the organizations of an oak, rose, dog and cat, and if he has the inclination and zeal to contract his human individuality down to the level of the life of a rose or a dog in order to comprehend and grasp completely the living being of the same, he may make the attempt, but he cannot expect it of others; better, let him try to expand his essence to the greatest individualities of a Cyrus, Moses, Alexander, Jesus, etc., or even only of the great orator Cicero, then it cannot fail that he will comprehend their necessity and will hold these individuals as well as the series of appearances of the world-spirit that one calls history to be more capable of a construction; but from the demand for the deduction of his pen he will for this purpose have to desist entirely and also make himself no further worry about idealism on account of ignorance in such things.
zh: 可笑的是，克鲁格先生毕竟还是这么宽宏，不想那么严格地跟那位摆出一副哲学大师架势的哲学家抠字眼；他只要求一点点东西，只要求从一个确定的表象作出演绎，例如月亮连同它的一切特征，或者一朵玫瑰、一匹马、一条狗，或者木头、铁、黏土、一棵橡树，或者干脆只要求从他的笔演绎出来。
看起来，克鲁格先生是想用这类要求让观念论者省事：他从太阳系里只挑出一个从属的点，即月亮，或者挑出还要容易得多的东西，即他的笔。
可是克鲁格先生难道不明白，在先验观念论里无法理解的那些规定性，属于自然哲学——他对于自然哲学与先验观念论的区别似乎一无所知——只要它们在哲学里谈得上（而克鲁格先生的那支笔则谈不上）？
在自然哲学里，他可以找到一种演绎（这个词在这里的含义和它的拼写一样不管用），即对他所提出的那些东西之一、对铁的演绎。
克鲁格先生对哲学建构的概念难道如此之少，竟以为月亮可以脱离整个太阳系被把握，而他对这个太阳系的表象又如此薄弱，竟看不出认识这个体系是理性最崇高、最高的任务吗？
如果克鲁格先生对这项确定任务的重大有所感觉，或者，如果他对当下首先关系到哲学的东西——也就是说，在人们长期把上帝摆在别的有限者旁边、或者干脆摆到最末尾当作一个从绝对有限性出发的公设之后，再一次把上帝绝对地置于哲学的开端，把他当作万物的唯一根据、当作唯一的 principium essendi 和 cognoscendi——哪怕只有一点遥远的预感，他怎么会想到要向哲学要求对他那支笔的演绎呢？

一条狗、一棵橡树、一匹马、一根芦苇，固然像摩西、亚历山大、居鲁士、耶稣等等一样，是更为优秀的东西，而这两类组织离哲学都比克鲁格先生的那支笔以及用那支笔写成的哲学著作更近；自然哲学会给他指出，他该怎样以概念把握一棵橡树、一朵玫瑰、一条狗和一只猫的组织，而如果他有意愿和热情，要把自己人的个体性收缩到一朵玫瑰或一条狗的生命那一阶段上，以便完全以概念把握和抓住它们活生生的存在，那他不妨去试一试，但不能要求别人也这样；他倒不如试着把自己的本质扩展到居鲁士、摩西、亚历山大、耶稣等等那些最伟大的个体性上，或者哪怕只扩展到那位大演说家西塞罗上，那就必定：他会以概念把握到他们的必然性，并且会认为这些个体以及那串被称为历史的世界精神的现象，更能够被建构；但为了这个目的，他必须完全放弃对他那支笔的演绎这一要求，并且也不必再为在这类事情上的无知而替观念论操更多的心。

en: Herr Krug believes that with this demand for the deduction of something so determinate he has made an extremely good find; he considers himself fully covered by it against idealism and thinks that through the solution of this problem the most recent idealistic system could be placed in safety against all further objections; he at least would have no scruple about immediately signing the whole system together with his deduced pen; but he is also convinced in advance that no idealist in the world will even make the attempt at it.
zh: 克鲁格先生相信，凭这项要求演绎某个如此确定的东西，他做了一个极好的发现；他觉得自己因此对观念论完全有了掩护，并且认为，只要解决了这个问题，最新的观念论体系就可以免受一切后续的反驳；至少他本人会毫不犹豫地连同他那支被演绎出来的笔一起给整个体系签字；但他同时也预先确信，世上没有一个观念论者会去做这个尝试。

en: So that one may understand his objection quite well, he sets out, for example from p. 34 onward, his common sense quite cosily in a series of naive problems which transcendental idealism would hardly be able to solve.

Such things are then that we are compelled to represent to ourselves that we were born at a determinate time, that we die at a determinate time, that we also daily receive news through newspapers of what is going on in the world there where we are not, etc. - That, if organization is a product of intelligence, one does not see how the natural scientist can come into regions where he discovers new plants, how he has need to travel the earth, etc., further not how intelligence can produce a person born blind, illness, death, - in short, it is quite inept not to count oneself among the fucos and yet to speak purely in this tone of the commonest common sense. - Herr Krug declares that no false shame keeps him from presenting his objections, he sincerely seeks the truth; because he absolutely cannot think an acting or doing without a being, "so I am", he says, "perhaps for that very reason absolutely incapable of philosophizing; but I cannot help its being so, and I would rather admit that incapacity than feign a conviction that I do not have"; - but the alternative is not present at all, either to feign or to pour common sense out over philosophy. - Besides these contradictions in the large, which Herr Krug discovers, that everything in transcendental idealism is to be deduced and yet the dogs and horses are not deduced, he finds still others, in that he puts together individual passages of the system in which quite different standpoints are spoken of and then, over the contradiction, as on p. 90, cries out with the words of the Jews: "Now what need we further witness, that our system is a dogmatic transcendent idealism? we have heard it from its own mouth."

For in the one passage that Herr Krug picks out, the talk is of the original boundedness, or of the fact that the I posits itself in opposition as subject and as object, whereby it is said that a system that sublates this ground would be a dogmatic transcendent idealism.

The other passage concerns the epoch of the development of self-consciousness in which the subjective and the objective separate for the I itself; for this point of separation the boundary lies neither in the I, which is now determined as subjective, nor in the thing, - it lies, if this is expressed, nowhere, it is absolutely because it is; it will appear, in relation to the I as well as to the thing, as absolutely contingent.
Herr Krug explains this thus: there is no ground of boundedness at all.
zh: 为了让人们把他的反驳理解得足够清楚，他从第 34 页起，比方说，相当惬意地把他的常识摆成一串天真的问题，说先验观念论恐怕解决不了这些问题。

这类事情就是：我们不得不表象我们是在某个确定的时间出生的，我们是在某个确定的时间死的，我们还每天通过报纸得到消息，知道我们不在的那些地方世界上发生着什么，等等。——还说，如果组织是智性的产物，人们就看不出自然研究者怎么能走到他发现新植物的那些地方去，他怎么有必要去游历大地，等等，也看不出智性怎么能产生一个天生盲人、疾病、死亡，——总之，不把自己算进 fucos 里去，却又纯粹用这种最庸俗的常识的腔调说话，实在是很不聪明。——克鲁格先生声明，没有任何虚假的羞耻阻止他提出自己的反驳，他真诚地寻求真理；因为他绝对无法设想一种没有存在的行动或作为，所以他说，“我大概正因为这个缘故而完全不适合做哲学；但我对此没有办法，我宁愿承认这种不适合，也不愿假装一种我并没有的信念”；——可是这里根本不存在非此即彼的选择：要么假装，要么把庸常知性往哲学上倒。——除了这些大的矛盾——克鲁格先生发现，在先验观念论里一切都该被演绎，而狗和马却偏偏没有被演绎——他还发现别的矛盾，办法是把体系里谈到完全不同的立足点的个别段落摆到一起，然后针对这个矛盾，像在第 90 页上那样，用犹太人的话喊出来：“我们何必再要见证，说我们的体系是一种独断的超验观念论呢？我们不是亲耳听它自己说过吗。”
因为克鲁格先生挑出的那一处，谈的正是原初的受限性，或谈的是自我在对立中把自己设定为主体兼客体，同时那里说，一个扬弃了这个根据的体系会是独断的超验观念论。
另一处涉及自我意识发展中的那个时期，在这个时期里，主观的东西和客观的东西对自我本身来说分开了；对于这个分离之点，界限既不在现在被规定为主观的那个自我里，也不在物里，——用话说出来就是，它不在任何地方，它绝对地存在，因为它存在；它就自我以及就物而言，都会显得是纯粹偶然的。
克鲁格先生是这样解释的：根本不存在受限性的根据。

en: From such pitiful stuff one sees that Herr Krug does not know even in the slightest the system which he declares it his duty to examine thoroughly before he dares to judge it publicly; otherwise, if he knew that consciousness was to be constructed, he could have known in advance, without looking about for a particular passage, that an action of the intelligence must occur in which the limit for the I and the thing appears as contingent, as without ground.
zh: 从这类可怜相可以看出，克鲁格先生对他宣称有责任先彻底审查、然后才敢公开评判的那个体系，连一星半点都不了解；否则，他若是知道意识是要被建构的，那么他不必去找什么特别的段落，事先就能知道：必定会出现一种智性的行动，在其中我与物的界限显得是偶然的、显得没有根据。

en: It remains to be mentioned, after we have shown Herr Krug's manner of examination, that at the end of the Letters on the Doctrine of Science, from p. 61 to the end, there is appended as an appendix a treatise on religious faith, and to this an appendix and again a supplement; the whole concerns Fichte's essays on religion.

Since Herr Krug here expressly declares - what he in general does without express declaration - that he intends to leave quite aside in this investigation the transcendental point of view, which can be proper only to the philosopher as such and which has, so he says, already been thoroughly examined by him (we find that Herr Krug has not spoken of it at all), we have nothing whatsoever to say about these outpourings of the heart and of sound common sense.

Especially penetrating are the outbursts of his fiery zeal against the heathens and their crassest superstition, which is said to be flatly contrary to the religion of good conduct; they are directed against the fact that in one of the essays in the Philosophical Journal it is said, with a certain boldness which, as Herr Krug thinks, is hardly compatible with the dignity of the subject: religion can just as well subsist with polytheism and anthropomorphism as etc.; to what absurdities, exclaims Herr Krug, can the craving to shine through paradoxes not seduce even a good head!
zh: 在我们展示了克鲁格先生的审查方式之后，还要提到一点：在《知识学通信》的结尾，从 S. 61 一直到末尾，作为附录附上了一篇论宗教信仰的文章，而这篇又附有一个附录、再附有一个补遗；整个东西涉及的是费希特论宗教的那几篇文章。
既然克鲁格先生在这里明确声明——他平时即便不明确声明也是这么做的——，说他要在这项研究里把先验的观点完全搁到一边，而这观点只可能属于哲学家作为哲学家，并且据说已经由他详细审查过了（我们发现，克鲁格先生根本就没有谈到过它），那么对于这些心肠和健全常识的倾泻，我们完全无话可说。
尤其咄咄逼人的，是他那股火热劲头对异教徒及其最粗陋的迷信所发的爆发——据说这种迷信与善良品行的宗教直接相悖；这些爆发针对的是：《哲学杂志》里有一篇文章，用了一种据克鲁格先生看来说不上与对象的尊严相容的大胆，说出这样的话：宗教与多神论、与神人同形论等等同样可以并存；克鲁格先生喊道，想出乖谬之论来炫耀的癖好，能把一个好头脑也诱到何等荒唐的地步啊！

en: As regards Herr Krug's own convictions, he calls for 'a special examination of them, since he is just now occupied with a new fundamental philosophy, in which such an examination might perhaps be of use to him'; it is only in the Letters on Transcendental Idealism and in the Organon that Herr Krug comes out with it, lat. urceus exit (but the actual amphora is to be a work on the whole of philosophy in 8 volumes, namely 7 volumes of content and one volume of index, for which Herr Krug hangs out the sketch of the Organon as a wreath).

In order to grasp these convictions at their centre, we take up what Herr Krug calls the main point of those convictions or his system; according to him there is in our consciousness (Organon, p. 75) an original transcendental synthesis between the real and the ideal, and the system which acknowledges and asserts this transcendental synthesis without wanting to explain it - because, in order to explain it, one would have to begin with the one or the other, and thus would have to sublate the synthesis itself - he calls transcendental synthetism, which is therefore transcendental realism and transcendental idealism in inseparable union. - These are words that do not sound bad.
It is only to be examined how Herr Krug actually understands that synthesis of the real and the ideal; for the word 'synthesis' does not make the thing.
Now the original synthesis, according to Organon p. 25, is consciousness; but consciousness is not the I, but is in the I.
zh: 说到克鲁格先生自己的信念，他要求 '对它们作一番特别的审查，因为他正好在忙着一门新的基础哲学，这样一种审查说不定对他还有用处'；直到《先验观念论通信》和《工具论》里，克鲁格先生才把这话亮出来，lat. urceus exit（不过真正的双耳瓶据说要是一部关于整个哲学的作品，共 8 卷，即 7 卷正文和 1 卷事项索引，克鲁格先生为它把《工具论》的草案当作一个花环挂出来）。
为了从中心把握这些信念，我们挑出克鲁格先生称为那些信念的要害或他的体系的那个东西；据说在我们的意识里（《工具论》，S. 75）有一种原初的先验综合，介于实在物与观念物之间；而那个承认并主张这种先验综合、却不愿去解释它的体系——因为要解释它，就得从这一方或那一方开始，因而就得把综合本身扬弃掉——，他称之为先验综合论，这也就是先验实在论与先验观念论不可分割的结合。——这些话听起来倒不坏。
只需考察一下，克鲁格先生究竟怎样理解那种实在物与观念物的综合；因为综合这个词并不就等于事情本身。
按照《工具论》S. 25，原初的综合就是意识；但意识并不是我，而是在我之中。

en: Let us hear Herr Krug further on the I; he is everywhere a warm patron of the I against the opponents of the Doctrine of Science, he has nothing against the I as the starting point of philosophy; all mockery of it is, he says, petty and insipid, etc.

With Herr Krug, however, the I separates itself off from reason, the two occur only in this narrative, the one as explanation of the other; otherwise, in the three works we have before us, so far as they have any relation to philosophy, the word 'reason' is likewise not used by Herr Krug; apart from the Letters on the Doctrine of Science, one finds it a few times in the genitive, or on p. 45 in a similar meaning - (on which we therefore also draw Herr Krug's attention, so that in the seven volumes of the philosophical sciences it may not befall him that reason occurs not at all or only in the genitive, and thus in the index, the 8th
volume, this thing would not be met with).

Herr Krug has sublated this coordination of 'I or reason', for reason could not be made into a thing; but that the I is a thing is one of the fundamental principles of this synthetism, which he proves frequently and diligently (p. 80 on transcendental idealism): where we perceive an acting, we must also assume an agent, that is, posit a subject of a certain reality, from which the acting, as it were, proceeds; or in the Organon: there is an I that is the subject of activity, for actual activity without a subject of activity cannot be thought, as, Herr Krug assures us, everyone's consciousness will teach him as soon as he wants to make the attempt to think such a thing.

That the principium essendi of cognition, or the real principle of cognition, is a cognizing subject - of this Herr Krug gives a kind of proof; for, he says, if no such subject were there, then no cognition would be there either.
zh: 我们再听听克鲁格先生关于我的进一步说法；他处处都是我的热心庇护人，用来对付《知识学》的反对者；他对把我看作哲学的出发点毫无异议；据他说，对此的一切嘲笑都是小心眼、都是乏味的，等等。
但在克鲁格先生那里，我与理性分开了，两者只在这段叙述里出现，一个充当另一个的解释；除此之外，在我们面前的这三部作品里，凡与哲学有关的地方，克鲁格先生同样没有用过理性这个词；除了《知识学通信》之外，只能偶尔碰见它出现在第二格，或者 S. 45 上有类似含义的用法——（我们为此也提醒克鲁格先生注意这一点，免得他在那七卷哲学科学里碰上这样的情况：理性根本不出现，或者只以第二格出现，于是在索引即第 8
卷里，压根就找不到这回事）。

克鲁格先生把'我或理性'这个并列给扬弃掉了，因为理性不能被弄成物；但我是一个物，却是这种综合论的基本原则之一，他常常并且着力地证明这一点（S. 80，论先验观念论）：凡是我们觉察到一种行动，也就必须假定一个行动者，也就是说，要设定一个具有某种实在性的主体，行动仿佛是从它那里发出的；或者在《工具论》里说：有一个我，它是活动的主体，因为没有活动主体的现实活动是无法设想的，克鲁格先生保证说，任何人只要愿意试着去设想这样的东西，他自己的意识就会教给他这一点。
说认识的 principium essendi 或认识的实在原则是一个认识着的主体，克鲁格先生为此给出了一种证明；因为他说，如果没有这样一个主体，也就不会有任何认识。

en: Now in this thing there is consciousness, and this consciousness is a collection of infinitely many things.

Herr Krug counts among them a principle of contradiction, a certain practical proposition, namely the moral law, further an Alexander who was a great hero, a Cicero who was a great orator, and infinitely many things of the like (S. 14), - all of them things that are all said not to be contained in the proposition I = I or A = A and are called manifold facts of consciousness.
These infinitely manifold facts of consciousness do indeed all lie in the I, into which they come in an incomprehensible way, but to be sure like a chaos without any unity and order:
zh: 那么，意识就在这个物里面，而这个意识是无限多事物的一个集合。
克鲁格先生从中数出一个矛盾命题、一个实践的命题，即道德法则，此外还数出一位伟大的英雄亚历山大、一位曾是伟大演说家的西塞罗，以及无限多诸如此类的东西（S. 14）——全是一些事物，据说它们都不包含在命题我 = 我或 A = A 里面，而且被称为杂多的意识事实。
这些无限杂多的意识事实虽然都在我之中，它们以一种不可理解的方式进入我，但确实像一团没有任何统一性和秩序的混沌：

en: Everything goes together higgledy-piggledy like mouse droppings and coriander.104)
zh: 一切都乱糟糟地混在一起，像老鼠屎和芫荽一样。104)

en: Then a reason in the genitive steps up and brings in, p. 76 f., a formal unity, arranges the confusion and connects by subordination under a certain principle as its point of unification - not as if from it all individual cognitions could and should be derived according to their content, but only the individual cognitions in their manifoldness are to be related to it as to a certain unity, just as in a vault everything relates to the keystone as the highest and last point of unification, although this point cannot at the same time contain in itself the foundation of the vault - and perhaps, Herr Krug thinks, the Doctrine of Science had precisely this in mind when it placed the proposition I = I at the head of its investigations, and this A = A would be a symbolic presentation of that harmony, the supreme formal fundamental proposition of philosophy, which, however, already presupposes other material fundamental propositions, facts of consciousness grasped in concepts and presented in propositions. - That 'perhaps' does honour to Herr Krug's caution; he certainly did not want to assert it.
zh: 这时就来了一个第二格的理性，在 S. 76 f. 上引进了一种形式的统一，把混乱整理好，并通过把诸多个别认识归摄于某个原则之下，使它们与这个原则、与这个作为统一点的东西联结起来；——并不是说，一切个别认识按其内容都能并且应当从这个原则中推导出来，而只是说，诸多个别认识在其杂多中应当被联系到它，把它当作某种统一，就像在一座拱顶建筑里，一切都联系到拱顶石这一最高、最后的统一点上，尽管这个点并不能同时把拱顶的基础包含在自身之内；——克鲁格先生认为，也许《知识学》把命题我 = 我置于其研究之首时，想到的正是这一点，而这个 A = A 会是那种和谐的象征性表述，是哲学最高的形式根本命题，但它已经以别的质料性根本命题、以被把握在概念中并表述在命题里的意识事实为前提了。——那个'也许'给克鲁格先生的谨慎增了光；他总归是绝不想把它断定下来的。

en: One sees now also that, when Herr Krug turned against transcendental idealism on account of original limitedness, he was not concerned with liberation from limitedness, but with finding in it a licence for the infinite multitude of the limitednesses of empirical consciousness and with showing that this system is not a hair better than his synthetism, which posits an infinite multitude of limitednesses of consciousness; Herr Krug for his part (Letters on Transcendental Idealism) holds that it by no means dishonours the philosopher to admit right from the outset that there are things that lie higher than all human wisdom; - to want to go out of one's consciousness and beyond it seems to him to amount to precisely this: to sublate one's consciousness and yet to want to keep it in the same act by which it is sublated. - But does Herr Krug understand by philosophical reflection anything other than the sublation of consciousness and the keeping of it in one and the same act?
zh: 现在也可以看出，当克鲁格先生因为原初的受限性而回过头来反对先验观念论时，他要的并不是从受限性中解放出来，而是要在其中为经验意识的无穷多受限性找到一张通行证，并表明这个体系并不比他的综合论好上一根头发，而他的综合论设定的正是意识的无穷多受限性；克鲁格先生这一边（《先验观念论通信》）认为，哲学家一开始就承认有些东西高过一切人类智慧，绝不丢脸；——想要走出自己的意识、超出它之外，在他看来说的正好是：把自己的意识扬弃掉，却又想在扬弃它的同一个行动中把它保留下来。——可是克鲁格先生所理解的哲学反思，难道不是意识的扬弃以及在同一且同一个行动中对该意识的保留，而是别的什么吗？

en: To make empirical consciousness the principle of his speculation - Herr Krug therefore believes himself fully entitled to that, and likewise to this, that what he finds in his empirical consciousness and must think in it is perfectly true; he must think the I as a thing, and therefore it is a thing.

We posit as actual that which we must think along with as necessary; thus have physicists and mathematicians proceeded in their sciences since the memory of man (p. 82), and no one to this day has yet called them to account for this procedure; indeed, even transcendental idealism proceeds in this way in a hundred places!

Why should it not be permitted to the opponents? ego homuncio non fecerim?105) - Only Herr Krug forgets that when mathematics, physics and idealism ask what must be thought, they do not turn to empirical consciousness, in which the dogs and cats, Herr Krug's pens and the great orator Cicero, etc., carry on their being. - According to what has gone before, Herr Krug's synthetism must be thought in the following way: one imagines a jug in which Reinholdian water, Kantian stale beer, enlightening syrup called Berlinism, and other such ingredients are contained as facts through some accident; the jug is the synthetic [unity] of these = I; now, however, someone steps up and brings a unity into that swill by separating the things, smelling and tasting one after another, or however that is to be done, chiefly hearing from others what has got in there, and then making a narrative about it; this one is now the formal unity, or philosophical consciousness.
zh: 把经验意识当作自己思辨的原则，克鲁格先生因此认为自己完全有理由这样做；他同样认为自己完全有理由主张：他在自己的经验意识里发现、并且不得不在其中思考的东西，是完全真的；他不得不把我当作物来思考，因此我就是一个物。
我们把不得不当作必然的东西一并思考进去的东西设定为现实的；物理学家和数学家自古以来在自己的科学里就是这么做的（S. 82），直到今天还没有人因为这个做法找过他们的麻烦；就连先验观念论也在上百处地方这么做！

为什么就不该允许反对者这么做呢？ego homuncio non fecerim?105)——只是克鲁格先生忘了：数学、物理学和观念论在问什么必须被思考时，并不去问经验意识，而在经验意识里，狗和猫、克鲁格先生的笔和那位大演说家西塞罗等等正在闹腾。——按前面所说的，克鲁格先生的综合论必须这样来设想：人们设想有一个罐子（Krug），里面因为某种偶然，作为事实装着赖因霍尔德式的水、康德式的陈啤酒、被称为柏林主义的启蒙糖浆，以及其他诸如此类的配料；这个罐子就是这些东西的综合物 = 我；这时却有一个人走上前来，往那锅杂烩里带进一种统一，办法是把那些东西分开，一件一件地闻一闻、尝一尝，或者看该怎么弄，主要是听别人说里面进去了些什么，然后对此作一番叙述；这个人就是那形式的统一，或者说哲学意识。

en: This is the essence of the Krugian synthetism, and, openly and undisguisedly as it lies there, it is not so easy to make out, since this system, as a true philosophical system must do, likewise comprehends all the others in itself: because being and thinking are united in empirical consciousness in an incomprehensible way, so that a genuine, sober and modest philosophy is not to go beyond it, Herr Krug takes his system to be at one with Jacobi's; the Kantian concepts a priori are not lacking in it, and, as we have seen, he is also a warm patron of the I of idealism.
zh: 这就是克鲁格式综合论的本质；它虽然摆得那么公开、毫不遮掩，却并不那么容易看出来，因为这个体系像一个真正的哲学体系必须做的那样，同时也把其他一切体系都包含在自身之内：由于存在和思维在经验意识中以不可理解的方式结合在一起，因此一种真正的、清醒而谦逊的哲学不该超出它去，克鲁格先生便认为自己的体系与雅可比的体系是一致的；康德那些 a priori 概念它也不缺；而且我们已看到，他也同样是观念论的那个我的热心庇护人。

en: Besides, as regards the historical consideration of what is proper to this system, one is necessarily reminded of the older, wholly identical system of Herr [C. C. E.] Schmid (Philosophisches Journal, year 1795, 10th issue

) (as the reviewer of the Organon in the Allgemeine Literatur-Zeitung [1801, vol. 3, no. 207] also remarks), a system of which one could not think that, after its very inventor had himself given up carrying it out, it should be awakened again out of its annihilation by another.
What Fichte at that time (Philosophisches Journal, year 1795, 12th issue106)

) already predicted has come about entirely: that this discovery would without doubt be made use of; only it is to be wished that those who make use of it would leave to the true inventor the honour of inventing and, as he would rather have it, the honour of finding, and would behave better toward him than toward another famous philosophical writer, whose writings are the true original source of their Kantianism, and to whom yet only few show the gratitude they owe. - Toward Reinhold, Herr Krug does not quite incur this fault of ingratitude, but he still does far from full justice to Reinhold.

In the Organon, p. 33, Herr Krug says that the Theory107), when it set up consciousness as the foundation of philosophical cognition, was not so far from the truth as some judges of it have asserted; but it erred only in this (Herr Krug has hit the right spot), that it presupposed that the whole of philosophical cognition must be built upon a single fact of consciousness or derived from it.

But Herr Krug in truth does the Theory wrong, for with the materiality of representations, which is also contained in that one principle of consciousness, the multitude of facts of consciousness must indeed come in, however infinitely manifold Herr Krug may demand it to be.
zh: 此外，就对这个体系本身所作的历史考察而言，人们必然会想起 [C. C. E.] 施密德先生那个更早、完全一样的体系（《哲学杂志》，Jahrg. 1795，10. Heft
）（正如《普通文学报》[1801, Bd. 3, Nr. 207] 上《工具论》的书评人也指出的），那是一个人们无法设想的体系：连它的发明者本人也放弃了实行之后，它竟会被另一个人从自己的毁灭中重新唤醒。
费希特当时（《哲学杂志》，Jahrg. 1795，12. Heft106）
）已经预言的事完全应验了：这项发现无疑会被人利用；只是但愿那些利用它的人，把发明的荣誉、以及他更愿意说的发现的荣誉，留给真正的发明者，并且对他比对待另一位著名哲学作家要好一些——那些人的康德主义，其真正源头就是这位作家的著作，可向他表示应有感谢的却只有少数人。——对赖因霍尔德，克鲁格先生倒没有完全犯下这种忘恩负义的过错，但他对赖因霍尔德还是远远没有完全公道。
在《工具论》S. 33 上，克鲁格先生说，理论107) 把意识树立为哲学认识的基础时，离真理并不像它的一些评判者所断言的那样远；它错只错在（克鲁格先生这回点到了正处）：它预先假定，全部哲学认识都必须建立在一个唯一的意识事实之上，或者从它推导出来。
不过克鲁格先生真正冤枉了理论，因为那个唯一的意识原则里也包含着表象的质料性，随着它，意识事实的繁多当然也就进来了，无论克鲁格先生要求它们多么无穷杂多。

en: Otherwise Fichte himself said of this system of synthetism that it corresponded excellently to the most urgent need of the time; the Kantian philosophy had caused a sensation, and many are looking for something special behind it.
Through that system all difficulties are removed at once; the world is there finished, without any contribution of reason.

Critical idealism receives a meaning so easy to grasp; through it nothing further is asserted than the capacity to bring our cognitions into a system. - Only this remains wonderful, after we have now received the disclosure, how so much clamour about nothing could have arisen, how Kant could have made such mighty preparations in order to demonstrate the very simple proposition that we can reason about the things in the world. - What was done at that time with regard to Kant, Herr Krug has accomplished for the Fichtean system, in that he shows that I = I means the principle of the original identity of the I, about which only the consciousness of ourselves can instruct us, which accompanies all my activities and through which I recognize them as my activity; in short, that the identity is to be placed in the fact that all facts of consciousness are in me and in no stranger. - Yet Herr Krug is content to present this explanation of I = I with a Perhaps, for "perhaps" I = I might also be supposed to express something else.
zh: 此外，费希特自己就说过，这种综合论体系极好地符合时代最迫切的需要；康德的哲学引起了轰动，许多人在它背后寻找某种特别的东西。
通过那个体系，一切困难一下子就被拿掉了；世界已经现成地在那里，理性的任何参与都不需要。

批判的观念论得到一个如此容易把握的含义；通过它，所主张的不外是那种把我们的认识带进一个体系的能力。——只是这一点仍然是奇妙的：在我们如今得到了这番说明之后，怎么会为了无物闹出这么大的声响，康德怎么会做出如此强大的准备，来证明我们可以对世界上的事物进行推理这个十分简单的命题。——当年针对康德所做的事，克鲁格先生为费希特体系做到了，他指明我 = 我意味着我的原初同一性的原则，关于这一点只有我们对自己的意识才能告诉我们，这种意识伴随我的一切活动，并且我借此把它们认作我的活动；总之，同一性就在于：意识的一切事实都在我之中，而不在任何一个外人之中。——不过克鲁格先生知趣地带着一个“也许”来提出对“我 = 我”的这种解释，因为“也许”我 = 我也可能该表示某种别的东西。

en: The foundation stone of this fundamental philosophy of his convictions Herr Krug lays out in detail in the 3rd

section, in which he proves that there must be only one real principle, the I, but several ideal principles; he appeals subsequently on pp. 19 and 77 to having demonstrated here the plurality of principles; yet the beginning of the concluding remark to this section on p. 15 reads thus: 'I therefore very much doubt that one [as Schelling thinks] will ever get out of the magic circle into which the investigation of the principles of philosophical cognition places us, through the assumption of a supreme absolute principle that expresses the entire content and the entire form of philosophy, etc.' (from Schelling, On the Possibility of a Form of Philosophy in General [Tübingen 1795, p. 18]).

If Herr Krug wants to found an 8-volume work of the philosophical sciences on this, how can his modesty and sobriety seduce him so far that, after he has proved the principle of his convictions, he only doubts the opposite principle?
zh: 克鲁格先生为他的信念的这套基础哲学详细地奠下基石，是在第 3

节里，他在其中证明，只应有一个实在原则，即我，但应有多个观念原则；他随后在第 19 页和第 77 页上援引说，他在这里已经证明了原则的多数性；然而这一节的结尾注释的开头，第 15 页上却是这样说的：“因此我十分怀疑，人们〔像谢林所认为的那样〕究竟是否会通过假定一个最高的绝对原则——它表达哲学的全部内容和全部形式等等——而从那种魔圈里走出来，哲学认识的原则的研究把我们带进了这个魔圈。”（引自谢林《论一种一般哲学形式的可能性》〔图宾根 1795 年，第 18 页〕）。
如果克鲁格先生想在此基础上建立一部 8 卷本的哲学科学著作，那么他的谦逊和清醒怎么会把他引诱到如此地步，以致在他已经证明了自己信念的原则之后，对那个相反的原则却只是怀疑？

en: With a main fact of consciousness, namely the external world, Herr Krug likewise gets no further than that he draws the result on p. 40 that, although the assumption of the reality of the external world cannot indeed be proved directly, yet indirectly, i.e. through reflection, very much can be said for the justification of that belief against the opposite assertion; namely this belief and presupposition is so necessary and natural to every human being that even the most decided idealist cannot free himself from it, for he believes in it as soon as he is not speculating. - And on p. 47 it follows precisely from this that the belief in the objective world is far more rational than the assertion of the opposite.
zh: 对于意识的一个主要事实，即外部世界，克鲁格先生同样也没有走得更远，他只是得出第 40 页上的结论：外部世界的实在性这一假定虽然不能直接被证明，但间接地，也就是通过反思，却可以针对相反的主张说出许多话来为那种信仰辩护；也就是说，这种信仰和前提对每个人来说都如此必要、如此自然，以致连最坚决的观念论者也不能摆脱它，因为只要他不作思辨，他就相信它。——而第 47 页上恰恰由此得出：对客观世界的信仰远比相反的主张更为合乎理性。

en: The simple and popular representations of philosophy that have been set out, such as a synthetism is, Herr Krug has squeezed into Spanish boots of real principles and formal ideal principles as well as material ideal principles, diligently cited Fichte's, Schelling's writings, the Philosophisches Journal, his own works, divided the whole into sections and special remarks no. 1, 2, 3 etc., and so on, - in short, by all such arrangements he has again taken away from the cause of his common human understanding a part of the popularity and comprehensibility that it has in and for itself and that constitutes a main merit of it so very much that, if this common human understanding brought into sections were really philosophy, our times and manners would be to be pitied, which do not permit one, as Socrates did, to turn directly to every distinguished and common man; Herr Krug would have to succeed in a short time in re-clothing the whole uneducated public as a philosophical one.

For the sceptics too this philosophy is excellent, as Herr Krug himself sees: "If I", he says, "have only correctly grasped and intelligibly presented the facts of my consciousness, then no philosopher in the world will be able to deny the principles set up by me; even the sceptic will have to admit them."
zh: 那些已经摆出来的关于哲学的简单而通俗的表象，如综合论就是这样的东西，克鲁格先生把它们塞进了实在原则、形式观念原则以及质料观念原则的西班牙靴子里，勤快地引用了费希特、谢林的文章、《哲学杂志》、他自己的著作，把整个东西分成节和专门的注释第 1、2、3 号等等，——总之，通过所有这类安排，他又从他这种健全常识的事情上拿掉了一部分它本身所具有的通俗性和易懂性，而这一点恰恰是它的主要功劳，以致如果这种被放进节里的健全常识现实地是哲学，那么我们就得为我们的时代和风尚感到惋惜了，它们不允许像苏格拉底那样径直去面向每一个高贵的人和普通的人；克鲁格先生想必很快就会成功，把整个未受教养的公众改换成哲学式的公众。
对怀疑论者来说这种哲学也是极好的，正如克鲁格先生自己所见到的：“如果我只是正确地领会并且明白易懂地表述了我意识的事实，”他说，“那么世界上就没有一个哲学家能够否认我提出的那些原则；连怀疑论者也不得不承认它们。”

en: If Herr Krug at the end of the organon (where we are also instructed that this organon is properly not yet the organon) indicates that, if his fundamental propositions should have the good fortune to receive the approval of the connoisseurs, he would not be disinclined to work out a system of philosophy in eight volumes, as he has already made known to his friends in a private announcement, - then on the one hand we merely give him to consider that in seven volumes a pretty number of facts of consciousness can indeed be set up, but that it is not to be seen how he could bring into them the infinitely manifold facts of philosophical consciousness, among which he also counts that "a great orator, named Cicero, a great warrior, named Alexander, has existed" etc.; - on the other hand, if seven volumes will not suffice for these facts, where is there still to be room left for philosophizing about these matters laid at the foundation, since the eighth volume, according to p. 112, is destined for the literature of philosophy and for an index of the philosophical matters of the seven volumes?
zh: 如果克鲁格先生在《工具论》的结尾（在那里我们还被告知，这部《工具论》其实还不是《工具论》）表示，如果他的根本命题有幸得到行家们的赞许，他就不反对写出一部八卷本的哲学体系，正如他已经在一次私人预告中向他的朋友们表示的那样，——那么我们一方面只是请他考虑：在七卷书里固然可以摆出相当数量意识的事实，但看不出他怎么能把哲学意识的无限杂多的事实也带进去，他甚至还把“曾有一位大演说家，名叫西塞罗，曾有一位伟大的战士，名叫亚历山大”等等也算在这些事实里；——另一方面，如果七卷书对这些事实还不够用，那么哪里还剩下空间来对当作基础摆在那里的这些事进行哲学思考，因为第八卷按第 112 页的说法是留给哲学文献和七卷中哲学事项的索引的？
